Saludos Amigos | Saludos Amigos (Spanish for "Greetings, Friends") is a 1942 American live-action animated package film produced by Walt Disney and released by RKO Radio Pictures. South of the Border with Disney | South of the Border with Disney is a 1942 Disney short documentary film.  It was shot in the same occasion "Saludos Amigos" was, when Walt Disney and a group of eighteen artists, musicians and writers went to South America looking for inspirations for a movie.  While "Saludos Amigos" is the result of this voyage, alternating animated shorts to the sequences from the travel that inspired them, "South of the Border with Disney" is more of a behind-the-scenes documentary showing only the travel and the genesis of cartoons not only for "Saludos Amigos" and "The Three Caballeros", but also some others used in later occasions.  The most notable example is a female Armadillo used for a 1943 Pluto cartoon, "Pluto and the Armadillo".  Film also includes some pencil test animation.
